## Task family: compare two noisy panels across a divider (task-fc84fd8d)

Evidence from two demonstrations (and a later unsolved test):

- Input is two same-size panels separated by a full-width/full-height solid divider row or column. Remove the divider; align the panels cell-by-cell. Output has the dimensions of one panel.
- At each aligned position, output `3` if the two input cells are equal. Otherwise output the panel's shared/background color (the common base color when both panels use one; in the horizontal demo, this was `5`, the bottom panel's background, while top background was `1`).
- Demo 1: horizontal divider color `4`, output 9x21 from 9x21 panels. Top panel colors 1/5 and bottom 5/2; output was 3 exactly where aligned cells matched (including 5/5 or other equal values), else 5.
- Demo 2: vertical divider color `7`, output 24x7 from 24x7 panels. Both panels use background 8, with noise colors 5 on left and 1 on right; output 3 at equal aligned cells and 8 where unequal. E.g. row 0 output starts `[3,8,3,3,8,8,8]`.

- Test that was over without solving: 21x15 input, divider row index 10, color 4; compare rows 0–9 to rows 11–20, producing 10x15. Top colors 2/6, bottom 5/2. A third demo confirmed the same direct equality comparison and clarified the color choice. The test was 9x23 with a solid divider column of `5` at 0-based column 11, so the left and right panels were each 9x11. Left panel used colors 4 and 6; right panel used colors 1 and 6.
